title: The Canal in Time: Before and After

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *antes de que* and *después de que* from B2 Unit 7. The history of the canal is a chain of events, so it is the natural place to use them. After *antes de que* the verb is always in the subjunctive; after *después de que* it is in the indicative when the event has happened, and in the subjunctive when it is still to come.

sections.title: Before and after, applied to the canal
rows: Antes de que existiera el canal, los barcos rodeaban América del Sur.
*antes de que* + imperfect subjunctive: before the canal existed, ships sailed round South America
Antes de que la obra se terminara, la empresa francesa quebró.
*antes de que* + imperfect subjunctive: before the work was finished, the company went bankrupt
Después de que Panamá se separó de Colombia, firmó un tratado con Estados Unidos.
*después de que* + indicative: something that happened
Después de que lleguen los barcos, se cerrarán las esclusas.
*después de que* + subjunctive: something still to come

items.spanish: Antes de que Panamá recibiera el canal, la Zona del Canal estaba bajo control estadounidense.
items.english: Before Panama received the canal, the Canal Zone was under American control.

items.spanish: Después de que se firmó el tratado de 1903, Estados Unidos empezó a construir el canal.
items.english: After the treaty of 1903 was signed, the United States began to build the canal.

items.spanish: Los barcos esperan en el mar antes de que se abran las esclusas.
items.english: The ships wait at sea before the locks open.

items.spanish: Después de que pase el barco, las esclusas se vuelven a llenar.
items.english: After the ship passes, the locks fill again.

sections.content: Ask the two questions you know. Who does the second action: the same person (*antes de salir*) or someone else (*antes de que salga*)? And for *después de que*: has it happened (indicative) or not yet (subjunctive)? *Antes de que* never takes the indicative.
